newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila urges court solution to Spratlys row.
newsitem.headline: Manila urges court solution to Spratlys row.

text.p: The Philippines urged on Tuesday international arbitration to solve a rancorous dispute with China over ownership of the Spratly islands in the South China Sea.
Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon said senior officials of the two countries in talks last week agreed "to lower the temperature" in their relations but stressed the need for further discussions.
"Later on I hope both would agree we would submit it to arbitration or to the ICJ," he told reporters, referring to the International Court of Justice in the Hague.
Siazon did not say which body should arbitrate or specify if he referred to the International Arbitration Court in Amsterdam.
Manila a few years ago filed a damage suit at the Amsterdam court against Westinghouse Electric Corp over a mothballed nuclear plant which the U.S. firm had built near Manila in the 1980s.

A long-standing row between the Philippines and China over the Spratlys - a cluster of potentially oil-rich isles and reefs - flared in April when Manila accused Beijing of sending armed naval ships near islands which Filipinos claim.
Beijing in turn protested against the hoisting of the Philippine flag over Scarborough Shoal, a pile rocks north of the Spratlys.
Tension rose after Manila two weeks ago arrested 21 Chinese fishermen off the shoal for alleged illegal entry.
Beijing insists everything in the South China Sea historically belongs to China. All or some of the Spartly islands are also claimed by Vietnam, Taiwan, Malaysia and Brunei.
